title: Fluent native Supabase authentication
objective: Implement native Windows Google sign-in through Supabase Auth with OAuth PKCE S256, system browser and secure loopback callback; validate Supabase JWTs cryptographically on the backend; and unlock the already-gated Gemini Cloud rewrite only for an authenticated, enabled and consented session while preserving the local default and keeping DeepSeek disabled.

included: Desktop Supabase public configuration read only from FLUENT_SUPABASE_URL and FLUENT_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY process environment variables, never from .env

Google OAuth authorization-code PKCE S256 through the system browser with a TcpListener bound only to 127.0.0.1 port 0, exact /callback path, random state, 8 KiB request cap, single terminal callback, timeout, cancellation and exact callback validation
Code exchange, session refresh, in-memory-only access tokens, Windows Credential Manager storage for refresh tokens, sign-out and single-flight refresh state
WPF sign-in, loading, cancel, signed-in identity, offline, expired, sign-out and truthful Cloud-mode presentation; consent remains separate and session-only
Desktop config validation requiring an HTTPS *.supabase.co URL plus nonempty publishable key before any browser, listener or network action

Backend cryptographic Supabase JWT validation through trusted-issuer OIDC discovery/JWKS cache and one-refresh retry, restricted to RS256/ES256 with exact configured issuer, exact authenticated audience, exp, nbf, role and subject validation

Backend migration of POST /v1/rewrite from the static FLUENT_BACKEND_TOKEN authenticator to default-deny Supabase JWT authentication, with fixed 503, 401, 403, 429, 400 and provider-503 ordering and per-validated-subject rate limiting
The sole direct dependency Microsoft.IdentityModel.Protocols.OpenIdConnect 8.19.2 in Fluent.Backend, central package version and dependency review evidence
Focused PKCE, callback, session, secret-store abstraction, Cloud gating, backend token/rate-limit, UI-state, no-secret, no-WebView and DeepSeek-inert tests
Architecture, ADR, privacy, phase, evidence, manual checklist, project state, roadmap and risk documentation
excluded: Any Supabase, Google Cloud, GitHub, provider or deployment account mutation, login, payment, publication or production deployment
Reading, modifying, printing, committing or loading .env, .env.*, secrets, credentials, keys, certificates, service-role values, JWT secrets, OAuth client secrets or provider API keys
WebView, embedded browser, OAuth confidential-client secret, password sign-in, account administration, user data synchronization, telemetry, live provider calls or automatic Cloud enablement
DeepSeek V4 Pro activation, selector, transport, model use, endpoint use or key use
Any change to local transcription, local rewriting, dictionary, insertion, hotkey, capsule, target identity, password protection or existing Fluent local data
Git add, commit, push, pull, reset, clean, checkout, switch, force action, registry edit or administrator installation

acceptanceCriteria: A desktop public client executes Google sign-in through the system browser with a one-time PKCE S256 verifier, constant-time random state, a TcpListener bound to ephemeral 127.0.0.1 /callback only, bounded request parsing, cancellation and no embedded OAuth secret.
Access tokens never persist; only refresh tokens are stored via an abstraction backed by Windows Credential Manager, and they are cleared on sign-out or definitive refresh rejection.

Desktop Cloud calls remain impossible unless authentication, Cloud enablement, session-only consent, backend availability and Gemini provider eligibility are all true; DeepSeek remains disabled, unselected and never called.

The backend uses only explicit valid FLUENT_BACKEND_SUPABASE_ISSUER and FLUENT_BACKEND_SUPABASE_AUDIENCE process configuration, binds OIDC metadata and JWKS to that trusted issuer, cryptographically validates Supabase asymmetric JWTs before dispatch, rejects missing, malformed, none/HS256/confused, invalid-signature, wrong-issuer, wrong-audience, expired, not-yet-valid, wrong-role and subjectless tokens, and rate-limits only valid subjects.

POST /v1/rewrite has documented default-deny response ordering: unavailable trusted verifier 503; missing/invalid token 401; valid token with wrong role 403; valid-subject quota denial 429; malformed rewrite 400; unavailable Gemini 503; success 200. The former static-token mechanism is removed from this route.
No secret, token, authorization code, verifier, user dictation or audio is logged, surfaced, committed or included in a distributed desktop configuration. .env is untouched and never read.

Focused adversarial tests cover state/code replay, duplicate/late/cancelled callbacks, callback size/path/state limits, malicious metadata/JWKS origin, kid rotation, cache outage, algorithm confusion, all required claims, refresh wipe, logging redaction and no-cloud-without-all-gates; full Release build, full suite, security/privacy/desktop/backend/adversarial reviews and final Development Judge evidence verdict pass; the result remains IMPLEMENTED_AWAITING_USER_REVIEW.
The live Supabase/Google smoke is documented but not attempted without explicit user authority and externally supplied public configuration.
requiredTests: PKCE verifier/challenge/state tests, constant-time state comparison, code/state replay rejection, callback listener 127.0.0.1-only/path/8-KiB/single-callback/duplicate/late/timeout/cancel tests and token exchange/refresh HTTP seam tests
Session single-flight, persistent refresh-token abstraction, access-token memory-only, sign-out, definitive-refresh wipe, offline-retention and expired-session tests
Cloud authorization gate and DeepSeek non-invocation regressions

JWT validation tests for missing/invalid trusted backend config, issuer/audience/JWKS-origin binding, RS256/ES256 allow-list, none/HS256/algorithm-confusion rejection, signature, exp, nbf, sub, role, unknown kid refresh-once, cache outage and fail-closed configuration
Backend POST /v1/rewrite 503, 401, 403, 429, 400 and provider-503 ordering plus per-validated-user rate-limit tests that prove no unvalidated header, raw token or address partitioning
Desktop presentation-state tests for sign-in, loading, cancel, signed-in identity, offline, expired and signed-out states
Repository scan tests for secrets, access-token persistence, token/code/verifier logging, WebView, static-token authentication and DeepSeek activation
requiredReviews: Desktop OAuth/PKCE and Windows credential-storage review
risks: OAuth callback interception, CSRF, authorization-code replay or PKCE verifier leakage.
Token persistence, logging or configuration could expose a credential.
An incorrect JWT verifier could accept forged, stale, symmetric or wrong-project tokens.
Rate limiting before authentication could let untrusted headers choose a partition.
Authentication work could accidentally relax the existing local-first, consent, exact-fallback or DeepSeek-disabled controls.
Missing external Supabase/Google settings can prevent live sign-in even if local verification passes.
rollbackPlan: Keep the existing default unauthenticated behavior available and revert the new authentication composition so RewriteContext remains LocalOnly.
Delete only the dedicated stored refresh credential through the application sign-out path; do not alter dictionary data or existing Fluent local data.
Remove the IdentityModel dependency and authentication code only after the full suite again proves the original local default.
dependencies: Phase 06B Cloud gate and Phase 07A Fluent rebrand remain implemented awaiting separate user reviews; neither is closed by this work.
Supabase project public URL/publishable key, Google provider enablement, loopback redirect allow-list and asymmetric signing keys are external prerequisites for a manual live smoke only.
Microsoft.IdentityModel.Protocols.OpenIdConnect 8.19.2 is the current supported OIDC/JWKS verification package evaluated for .NET 10; restore requires ordinary package-network availability.
humanApprovals: The user explicitly directed Phase 07B Native Authentication with Supabase, selected Google sign-in, required PKCE S256 and system browser, and explicitly excluded Clerk and DeepSeek activation.
No authorization is present for account login, Supabase/Google configuration, deployment, live provider invocation or Git publication.
